## 6-Week Data Analysis Certificate Prep Plan

A beginner-friendly plan built for **free resources only**, with weekday study blocks of **1.5 hours** and a **4-hour Saturday session**. It focuses on building core skills first, then moving into practice and timed revision.

## Weekly Study Roadmap

| Week | Focus | Weekday Plan (1.5h/day) | Saturday Plan (4h) | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Spreadsheets basics | Interface, formulas, cell references, functions | Build a simple budget sheet; practice formulas | Navigate and calculate confidently |
| 2 | Data cleaning | Sort/filter, remove duplicates, text cleanup, missing values | Clean a messy dataset from start to finish | Turn raw data into usable data |
| 3 | Basic statistics | Mean, median, mode, range, percent, simple distributions | Solve practice questions using spreadsheet formulas | Interpret common stats correctly |
| 4 | Charts and visualization | Bar, line, pie, histogram basics; choosing the right chart | Create charts from cleaned data and explain them | Match chart type to question |
| 5 | Interpreting results | Trends, outliers, comparisons, conclusions, limitations | Work through case studies and short written answers | Explain what data means clearly |
| 6 | Full revision and mock exam | Mixed review, weak areas, flashcards, timed drills | 1 full mock exam + review mistakes | Build exam readiness and speed |

## Week-by-Week Study Plan

### Week 1: Spreadsheets Foundations
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/laptop.svg
- Weekdays: Learn spreadsheet layout, formulas, relative vs absolute references, SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX.
- Saturday: Create a small tracker such as expenses, attendance, or study hours.
- Output to aim for: a clean worksheet with at least 10 formulas and correct formatting.

### Week 2: Cleaning Messy Data
- Weekdays: Practice sorting, filtering, removing duplicates, trimming spaces, and handling blanks.
- Saturday: Take one messy dataset and clean it step by step.
- Output to aim for: one before/after dataset with notes on what changed and why.

### Week 3: Basic Statistics
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calculator.svg
- Weekdays: Review mean, median, mode, range, percentages, and simple interpretation.
- Saturday: Use spreadsheet formulas to calculate stats on a small dataset.
- Output to aim for: quick calculation of core statistics without help.

### Week 4: Charts and Visual Storytelling
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/bar-chart.svg
- Weekdays: Learn when to use bar, line, pie, and histogram charts.
- Saturday: Build 3–4 charts from one dataset and label them clearly.
- Output to aim for: charts that are readable and correctly chosen for the data.

### Week 5: Interpreting Results
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/chat-left-text.svg
- Weekdays: Practice writing 3–5 sentence conclusions from charts and tables.
- Saturday: Answer short case-study questions and explain findings in plain language.
- Output to aim for: clear conclusions plus at least one limitation or caveat.

### Week 6: Final Revision and Mock Exam
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/journal-check.svg
- Weekdays: Review weak topics, redo errors, and complete timed mini-quizzes.
- Saturday: Take one full mock exam under timed conditions, then review every mistake.
- Output to aim for: stable score on practice tests and fewer repeated errors.

## Revision Strategy That Works

- Use a **3-pass review system**:
  - Pass 1: Learn the concept
  - Pass 2: Practice with a dataset
  - Pass 3: Explain it in your own words without notes
- Keep a **mistake log** with 3 columns:
  - Topic
  - What went wrong
  - Correct rule or fix
- Review the mistake log every **Saturday evening or Sunday**.
- Spend the last **15 minutes of each weekday** on recall:
  - 3 formulas
  - 1 chart choice question
  - 1 interpretation question

## Progress Tracking Method

Use a simple free scorecard in a spreadsheet or notebook.

| Metric | How to Measure | Target by Exam Week |
|---|---|---|
| Spreadsheet accuracy | Correct formulas in practice tasks | 90%+ correct |
| Cleaning speed | Time to clean a sample dataset | Faster with fewer errors |
| Stats recall | Answer from memory | 8/10 correct |
| Chart choice | Pick the right chart for a scenario | 8/10 correct |
| Interpretation | Write a clear 3–5 sentence conclusion | Clear, evidence-based answers |
| Mock exam score | Full practice test result | Consistent passing score |

### Weekly Self-Check
- End of each week, rate yourself 1–5 on:
  - Understanding
  - Speed
  - Accuracy
  - Confidence
- If any area is below 3, use the next Saturday session to fix it first.

## Free Resources and Practice Ideas

- Use **Google Sheets** or **LibreOffice Calc** for spreadsheet practice.
- Practice with free sample datasets from:
  - public government data portals
  - Kaggle free datasets
  - data from CSV files you create yourself
- Use free tutorials and docs for formulas, charts, and cleaning basics.
- Create your own mock questions from real datasets to simulate exam tasks.
